To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have produced a highly specific immunotoxin against a human breast cancer antigen and that this conjugate can kill tumor cells in vitro and reduce the tumor take in a mouse model in vivo.
we have produced an immunoconjugate with a high level of specificity for a human breast carcinoma cell line and that we have demonstrated its potential therapeutic efficacy in a xenogenic model.
we have produced a conjugate between a plant toxin, the ribosome inactivated protein restrictocin (res), and a monoclonal antibody (mab), MBr1, that recognizes a breast tumor antigen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of immunoconjugates between monoclonal antibodies and ribosome inactivators, in particular with the generation of a MBr1-Restrictocin conjugate.
the preparation of a conjugate between a monoclonal antibody (MAb), MBr1, directed against human breast cancer and the ribosome inactivation protein (RIP) restrictocin (RES).
the development of a new class of immunoconjugates, which are based on the association of monoclonal antibodies with ribosome inactivators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Res-MBr1 conjugate is a promising tool for the treatment of human breast carcinoma.
the MBr 1-Res conjugates are not yet ready for clinical trials.
the Res-MBr1 conjugate is capable of reducing the take of a breast carcinoma xenograft.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MBr-1/Res immunoconjugate has been prepared and tested for its cytotoxic activity on a cell line expressing the relevant antigen.

the use of a ribosome-inactivating protein, coupled to a monoclonal antibody with a quite restricted specificity for human breast carcinoma (MBr1), was tested on a cell-free system and on different cell lines in vitro.
we have shown that a plant toxin can be coupled to a monoclonal antibody and that the resulting conjugate has a cytotoxic effect on a tumor cell line which expresses the relevant antigen.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a plant toxin as a cytotoxic moiety in a conjugate with an antibody directed against a tumor cell surface antigen may be a valid approach, provided that the antigen is internalized and that a sufficient amount of conjugate is internalized.
we can use a plant toxin, restrictocin, to prepare a highly specific conjugate for breast carcinoma cells.

the conjugation between a toxin and a monoclonal antibody is not sufficient to guarantee an efficient cytotoxicity and that the use of a toxin as a targeting molecule must be evaluated in the light of the peculiarities of the molecule itself.
